performance_tasks.brief: A Paper 3 Question 1 style task (20 marks): an experiment described in words, with a set of our readings of the independent and dependent variables. The learner says how each reading would be taken and repeated, draws up the table (quantity / unit headings, a calculated column, consistent raw data, justified significant figures), plots the graph on their own graph paper against the stated conditions, finds the gradient and the intercept, and uses them to find the constants of a given equation, with units.
performance_tasks.objective_ids: choose 2-4 objectives from this topic that the task genuinely exercises

performance_tasks.brief: A Paper 3 Question 2 style task (20 marks): an experiment described in words whose method is deliberately inaccurate, with two sets of our readings. The learner estimates an absolute uncertainty from repeats and turns it into a percentage uncertainty, calculates a constant twice and tests a suggested relationship against a criterion they state first, then gives four limitations and four improvements, each tied to the measurement it affects.
performance_tasks.objective_ids: choose 2-4 objectives from this topic that the task genuinely exercises

performance_tasks.brief: A second Paper 3 Question 1 style task (20 marks), set in a different area of physics from the first (if the first is mechanical, this one is electrical, optical or thermal): the same table, graph, gradient, intercept and constants, from a different experiment described in words with our readings.
performance_tasks.objective_ids: choose 2-4 objectives from this topic that the task genuinely exercises

performance_tasks.brief: A second Paper 3 Question 2 style task (20 marks), in a different area of physics from the first: an inaccurate method with two sets of our readings, a percentage uncertainty, a test of a suggested relationship against a stated criterion, and four limitations with four matching improvements.
performance_tasks.objective_ids: choose 2-4 objectives from this topic that the task genuinely exercises

ao_mix_note: The syllabus states its AO weights as a share of MARKS, so planned_ao_mix_by_marks is the one that answers "does this resource match the exam". It values each card at the tariff of the question it models, split across the AOs the card declares, and values each performance task at the marks of the paper part it models. The count-based mix below is reported only because it is what a reader expects to see; do not balance against it. AO shares by ITEM COUNT: Every objective needs one recall anchor, so AO1 has a structural floor of about 31% in this topic (40 objectives against 131 slots) and cannot reach the 40% target by count however many other cards are added - padding the bank to chase it makes the resource worse. The framework already measures the AO4 share in practice time rather than by count for the same reason. Treat AO1 above target as expected, and AO2/AO3/AO4 below target as the thing worth fixing.
